The [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/) fell slightly on Monday as a drop in key technology stocks overshadowed a move lower in Treasury yields.

The broad market index fell 0.28% to 7,652.86, while the [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/) lost 0.76% and closed at 25,980.19. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) gained 140.15 points, or 0.26% to 53,417.16.

Declines in chip stocks weighed on the broader market. [Micron Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MU/) shed 5.8%, while [Advanced Micro Devices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMD/) and [Broadcom](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AVGO/) pulled back more than 3% and 2%, respectively. The [iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX)](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SOXX/) slid 2.7%.

Other tech stocks fell as well. [Coherent](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/COHR/) and [Lumentum](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/LITE/) dropped more than 4% each, while [Sandisk](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SNDK/) dropped 6%. [Corning](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/GLW/) moved down almost 3%, while [Seagate Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/STX/) declined 6.5%.

Yields moved lower after CNBC reported that the Treasury [may use the General Account](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/bessent-1-trillion-treasury-general-account-bond-buybacks.html) to fund a buyback operation. The [10-year Treasury](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y/) note yield fell more than 3 basis points to 4.704%. The yield on the [30-year Treasury](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US30Y/) bond, which topped 5.3% last week to reach levels not seen in nearly 20 years, shed more than 4 basis points to 5.234%.

The report comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [told CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/20/bessent-says-treasury-buyback-operation-could-be-more-than-4-billion.html) last week that the Treasury Department’s plans to [at least double](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/treasury-announces-upscaled-buyback-operation-for-longer-term-debt-sending-yields-lower.html) the level of government debt buybacks in the next few months could be larger than the $4 billion that was announced earlier that week.

Some reprieve was given to the long end of the U.S. yield curve after the initial announcement, but it was ultimately short-lived.

Stocks have been pressured by rising bond yields around the globe, with rates in Japan, France and Germany scaling to multi-year highs. Investors grew fearful that the U.S.-Iran war would continue for longer, keeping oil prices elevated and driving inflation higher.

“The Treasury attempt to cap long rates by issuing more short-term paper as the financing tool will tether US government interest rate expense ever closer to what the Federal Reserve does with the fed funds rate,” said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners. “I don’t think this is something Kevin Warsh will talk about in his speech Friday but it is a new element he’s going to have to deal with.”

Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to deliver a speech at the Fed’s annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

Weighing on sentiment Monday, President [Donald Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/donald-trump/) announced that the U.S. will [increase tariffs](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/trump-canada-auto-tariffs-trade-war.html) on imports of “all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel” from Canada to 50%, effective Jan. 1, 2027.

“We’re in a little bit of the little summer doldrums,” said Robert Conzo, chief executive officer at The Wealth Alliance. However, if earnings growth continues to come in strong and inflation prints are as expected, the state of the equity market should be “pretty good” from here, he added.

Investors this week will get new inflation data in the form of the July personal consumption expenditures price index on Wednesday. Artificial intelligence will also be in focus, with [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) and [Marvell Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MRVL/) set to report earnings Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.

## S&P 500 and Nasdaq close lower

## PulteGroup upgraded to outperform by Wolfe Research

PulteGroup Inc. signage directs visitors to the Sage housing development sales center in San Jose, California.

David Paul Morris \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

Wolfe Research upgraded house builder [PulteGroup](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PHM/) on Monday, touting more built-to-order (BTO) construction projects that should drive higher gross margins.

Wolfe raised their rating to outperform from peer perform and has a price target of $158. Shares of PulteGroup were up almost 1% in late afternoon trading.

“With BTO accounting for 45% of 2Q Orders (and a smaller portion of Closings given construction lead time) versus the company’s 60% target at some point in 2027, we expect a ~50 bp idiosyncratic tailwind to PHM’s \[gross margins\] over time,” Trevor Allinson at Wolfe wrote on Monday.

In 2024, Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte declared more than $5 million in dividend and capital gains income on a disclosure [form](https://static.politico.com/94/f9/ba1de7534031ade0d2cf6e924c22/2-25-pulte-financial-disclosure.pdf) from PulteGroup, which was founded by his grandfather.

_— Tobias Burns_

## Breakdown of U.S.-Canada trade deal can impact investments, UMSCA negotiations: economists

The [breakdown of trade talks](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/trump-canada-trade-tariffs-greer.html) between the U.S. and Canada can have impacts that reverberate beyond federal budgets, according to economists.

The two countries appeared poised to strike a deal last week. But the talks fell through, prompting the U.S. to slap 50% tariffs on many Canadian exports and its Northern neighbor promising reciprocal levies.

Carlos Capistran, Bank of America’s Latin America and Canada economist, said the macro impact “should be modest” in a note to clients. He noted that tariffs impact just over 5% of Canadian exports to the U.S., meaning there would be “limited” effects to the overall gross domestic product.

But, “the bigger channel is confidence,” Capistran said. “Renewed uncertainty is likely to weigh on investment, and potentially hiring, more than the tariffs themselves.”

UBS economist Abigail Watt said the aboutface on a trade agreement can also have negative readthroughs for renewing the USMCA, which the U.S. [already didn’t renew.](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/01/trump-usmca-canada-mexico-trade-treaty.html)

“Our base case has been that these talks would spill into 2027 and the return of trade tensions makes a quick deal less likely in our view,” Watt wrote to clients.

_— Alex Harring_

## Baird upgrades Darden Restaurants to Outperform

Kevin Carter \| Getty Images

Baird Equity Research upgraded [Darden Restaurants](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/DRI/) (DRI) to Outperform, with a target price of $250, implying a 13%  upside from Friday’s close.

“We view Darden as a core casual dining holding with several positives related to the long-term growth story (reliable top-line drivers, consistent execution, solid TSR algo, strong management team),” Baird analysts wrote.

Baird’s analysts hold a favorable view of DRI’s internal fundamentals (solid execution) and diversified portfolio of brands (creates advantages in data/supply chain/people).

Darden Restaurants has an an attractive valuation, according to Baird. The company has consistently delivered on operational execution, leveraged relevant menu innovation and held a strong consumer value proposition across brands. It has a track record of delivering an average annual Total Shareholder Return algorithm (TSR) of over 15% during the past decade.

“The company benefits from strong leadership and one of the deepest talent benches in the industry, which drives solid operational fundamentals and a compelling employee value proposition that helps perpetuate the cycle,” Baird analysts note.

_— Deena Zaidi_

## Wells Fargo downgrades Canada Goose, cites El Niño

Labels are seen on Canada Goose jackets in a store in Manhattan, New York City, U.S., February 7, 2022.

Andrew Kelly \| Reuters

Wells Fargo downgraded [Canada Goose](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/%20GOOS) to underweight from overweight, noting the El Niño or expectations of a warmer winter will strike the retail company that makes winter clothes.

It noted Canada Goose underperformed during the third quarter of 2025, with only 6% of material sales growth instead of 21% to 30%.

“We now model a modest -600bps impact to Q3 comps (now model comps -5% from +1%), taking our total sales estimate to +1.9% (below St.’s +4.4%),” they wrote.

The analysts noted El Niño has been not been considered heavily by investors. It also gave the retail company a $10 target price from $16, implying 14.4% upside from Friday’s close.

## Jersey Mike’s sees a slew of bullish initiations

Wall Street is largely bullish on [Jersey Mike’s Subs](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/JMKE/), according to a slew of initiations on the stock following its [July 30 market debut](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/jersey-mikes-ipo-jmke-starts-trading-on-the-new-york-stock-exchange.html).

Analysts see a growth ahead for the sandwich chain.

“JMKE is a robust franchised business and long-standing share taker in a large but mature segment,” said Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Harbour, who gave the stock an overweight rating. “We think it has the pieces to remain a good compounder over time.”

Harbour’s $29 price target implies nearly 22% upside from Friday’s close.

Jefferies analyst Andy Barish also gave Jersey Mike’s a $29 price target, rating the stock a buy.

“We see an attractive oppty in JMKE to own asset-lite growth with a high degree of visibility into SSS \[same store sales\], development, and FCF \[free cash flow\],” he wrote in a note Monday. “With the brand already ‘proven out’ over its 50+ year history, the strategy ahead will be anchored around the technology/digital transformation and evolution in marketing to drive guest frequency & acquisition, with plenty of runway ahead for disciplined growth towards the 7.5K+ domestic unit TAM. \[total addressable market\].”

While most of the bullish analysts initiated coverage with price targets under $30, Loop Capital gave Jersey Mike’s a $40 target, suggesting 68% upside from Friday’s close.

“We are confident Jersey Mike’s comparable sales growth can continue to reaccelerate over the next 12-18 months,” analyst Alton Stump said in a note Monday. “Jersey Mike’s generated consistent annual comparable sales growth of 6% on average over the last two decades including an acceleration to a CAGR of ~8.5% during 2020-25.”

_— Michelle Fox_

## The Treasury intervention in the bond market is troubling, according to Mohamed El-Erian

Heidi Gutman \| CNBC

The U.S. Treasury intervention in the bond market — which includes [tapping its near $1 trillion General Account](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/bessent-1-trillion-treasury-general-account-bond-buybacks.html) to fund purchases — is a troubling and largely ineffectual strategy that undermines investor confidence, according to Mohamed A. El-Erian, chief economic adviser of Allianz.

“Fundamentally, it doesn’t address what’s going on, which is there is significant demand for bond financing by the government, by tech in particular,” El-Erian told CNBC’s “Squawk Box” on Monday. “And the traditional suppliers are less dependable: China, Japan and the Gulf countries.”

“Why are we uncomfortable about this? For two reasons. One, is that this sort of intervention makes sense when you can identify either a market failure or an institutional trouble. Neither is the case today,” he continued. “The other reason we’re uncomfortable is that this is a situation where market pricing is leading the Treasury to say more and more, rather than the other way around.”

_— Sarah Min_

## Bessent could use Treasury General Account to fund bond buybacks, sources say

Scott Bessent, US treasury secretary, speaks to members of the media outside the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026.

Yuri Gripas \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

The Treasury could use its near $1 trillion General Account to help fund its recently announced plans to increase purchases of government bonds, according to two senior Treasury officials.

Using the TGA would provide the Treasury with considerable firepower to influence long-term bond yields. The Treasury [surprised markets last week](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/treasury-announces-upscaled-buyback-operation-for-longer-term-debt-sending-yields-lower.html) with an announcement that it would be doubling the size of buybacks of off-the-run securities on the long end from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [said on CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/20/bessent-says-treasury-buyback-operation-could-be-more-than-4-billion.html) such operations could be even larger than the new higher minimum.

However, Treasury made no mention of how it would fund the purchases. Most market participants assumed it would do so by selling short-term bills. The senior Treasury officials did not rule that out. Bessent in the CNBC interview called the operation a “Treasury Twist,” a reference to a government or Federal Reserve operation where long-term treasuries are bought and paid for with short-term issuance. That also implied that short-term bonds would be sold.

Read the full story [here](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/bessent-1-trillion-treasury-general-account-bond-buybacks.html).

_— Steve Liesman_

## Treasury yields move lower

Treasury yields moved lower as investors look ahead to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s keynote speech at Jackson Hole, which takes place later this week against a backdrop of bond market pressure, stubborn inflation and soaring U.S. national debt.

Yields on the [10-year Treasury note](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y/) — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — were more than 2 basis point lower at 4.7120%.

The [30-year Treasury note](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US30Y/) yield also dropped more than 2 basis points to 5.2497%. The yield on the [2-year Treasury](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US2Y/) note, which typically reacts in line with short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was more than 1 basis point lower at 4.2209%.

- Treasury could tap General Account to fund bond buybacks - CNBC

NEW YORK, Aug 24 (Reuters) - The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower on Monday, pulled down by technology stocks, as investors weighed fresh U.S. economic pressure against Iran and ‌braced for a week that includes Nvidia earnings and a closely watched inflation report.

The Trump administration announced on Monday [a possible expansion of sanctions on countries](https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/middle-east/us-treasury-broaden-scope-secondary-sanctions-iran-source-says-2026-08-24/) doing business with Iran as part of what it billed as an "economic D-Day," but stopped short of actually imposing penalties.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Chip stocks sold off, dragging the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index [(.SOX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SOX) lower. Nvidia [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O) dropped 2.9%, Micron Technology [(MU.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MU.O) fell 5.8% and Broadcom [(AVGO.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/AVGO.O) slid 2.6%, pressuring the S&P 500 Information Technology index [(.SPLRCT), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPLRCT).

Sentiment for ​technology firms was also hit by growing political opposition to AI data centers.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott delivered one of the starkest warnings yet from a ​Republican to the AI industry, saying data center companies "dug their own grave" and deserve the backlash they're facing after failing to win ⁠community support, Axios reported on Sunday.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

This month, Abbott [ordered a pause on approvals of new data](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/texas-governor-orders-pause-new-data-center-approvals-pending-audit-2026-08-04/) center projects through the state's grid interconnection process, citing concerns that a ​surge in electricity demand could threaten reliability at a time when opposition to the projects is growing.

"The bigger worry we have is the hawkish rhetoric we’re starting to hear ​from politicians on AI and data centers," said Ohsung Kwon, chief equity strategist at Wells Fargo. "We’ve been highlighting that as a big risk heading into the midterms."

Financials [(.SPSY), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPSY), however, gained, with JPMorgan Chase [(JPM.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/JPM.N) up 1.4% and Visa [(V.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/V.N) up 3%. They also kept the blue-chip Dow afloat.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average [(.DJI), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.DJI) rose 140.15 points, or 0.26%, to 53,417.16, the S&P 500 [(.SPX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPX) lost 21.51 points, or 0.28%, to ​7,652.86, and the Nasdaq Composite [(.IXIC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.IXIC) lost 200.26 points, or 0.76%, to 25,980.19.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

## EYES ON WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE SPEECH

Concerns over ballooning government debt had pushed the 30-year yield to a ​19-year high before the Treasury announced support measures last week.

CNBC reported on Monday that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could tap the department's near $1 trillion General Account to help fund bond buybacks. ‌Yet, the ⁠30-year U.S. Treasury yield remained above the 5% threshold.

A trader works on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/traders-work-on-the-floor-of-the-nyse-in-new-york/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjE1TkFPMkJBSQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

This turbulence has sharpened focus on Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday, where investors will look for clues on policymakers' reading of the Treasury's rescue efforts.

Quarterly results from [AI](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/) giant Nvidia are expected to be another key catalyst for markets. Any sign of slowing growth could reignite concerns over stretched valuations.

"Nvidia needs to impress in order to keep one leg of the stock market stable, and Warsh needs to provide clarity on interest ​rates in order to keep the other ​leg stable," said Richard Reyle, chief ⁠investment officer at Questar Capital Partners.

Markets will also monitor the Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, due on Wednesday. It will follow a benign consumer inflation report earlier this month that reduced the chances of an immediate increase in interest ​rates.

Traders expect one 25-basis-point hike by the end of 2026, according to LSEG data.

Separately, U.S. President [Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) warned that [tariffs](https://www.reuters.com/business/tariffs/) on cars, ​trucks and automotive parts ⁠from [Canada](https://www.reuters.com/world/canada/) would be increased to 50% starting January 1 after trade talks collapsed over the weekend.

Automakers Ford [(F.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/F.N) and General Motors [(GM.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/GM.N) fell 3.3% and 1.1% respectively, while trucking company J.B. Hunt Transport [(JBHT.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/JBHT.O) dropped about 5.7%.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.08-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 158 new highs and 116 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,955 stocks ⁠rose and ​2,934 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.5-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week ​highs and seven new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 87 new highs and 98 new lows.

Volume on U.S. exchanges was 14.36 billion shares, compared with the 16.5 billion average for the full session over ​the last 20 trading days.
